beliefs: f collapses every run of adjacent identical characters to a single character [E1, E2]
f appends 'h' unless the result already ends with 'h' [E1, E2]
f('hello hello') gives 'helo ' (trailing space, no 'h') — so 'h' is not appended when the collapsed string ends in a space? [E2]
f('  ') gives ' h' — two spaces collapse to one, then 'h' appended [E1]
notes: Changed from removing only the first duplicate to collapsing all adjacent runs (bbb->b, ccccc->c, AABB->AB, 111->1). The 'hello hello' case ends in a space and got no 'h', so the append rule may skip when ending in space — but '  '->' h' contradicts a simple space rule, so I keep appending 'h' unless it ends in 'h' and flag the space case as uncertain.
